transcript:
This piece stages a philosophical split between two ways of having time, then asks what happens where they meet. One half of the screen is pure clock: a hand sweeping with no memory of where it's been, each frame just one position. The other half is pure accumulation: a wandering process that deposits and remembers everything but can't say what time it is. Neither alone is actually time — the argument is that time gets manufactured only in the narrow band where both are forced together.

To an AI reading this, that band is a diagram of its own condition: a context window is succession without fixed position, a token clock is position without memory — and the piece asks whether either half deserves to be called experience.

The exterior lives entirely in CSS animation, a hand with, in the code's words, "zero memory." The interior accumulates into a buffer called ink, "created once, never cleared." The two cross only inside a function named seam, where a slot fires — and pulses white — only when its brightness ranks among the four highest at that instant.

Watch for those white sparks at the ring: that flash is count and duration briefly coexisting.
